questions.question: A does half as much work as B in three-fourth of the time. If together they take 66 days to complete the work, how many days shall B alone take to do it?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of efficiencies of A and B = (1/2) ÷ (3/4) = 2 : 3.

Total combined efficiency = 2 + 3 = 5 units/day.

Total work = Combined efficiency × Total days = 5 × 66 = 330 units.

Time taken by B alone = Total work ÷ Efficiency of B = 330 ÷ 3 = 110 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 110 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A does half as much work as B in three-fourth of the time.

Together they complete the work in 66 days.

**Formula Used:**

Total Work = Efficiency × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let B take x days to complete the whole work.

⇒ A completes half the work in (3/4)x days.

⇒ Time taken by A for full work = 2 × (3/4)x = 1.5x days.

⇒ Let Total work = LCM of 1.5x and x = 3x units.

 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

⇒ Combined efficiency of A and B = 2 + 3 = 5 units/day.

⇒ Time taken together = Total work ÷ Combined efficiency

⇒ 66 = 3x ÷ 5

⇒ 3x = 66 × 5

⇒ 3x = 330

⇒ x = 110 days.

⇒ B alone takes x = 110 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 110 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Time and Work Relation

Work = Efficiency × Time. Efficiency and time are inversely proportional when the total work is constant.

Work and Wages

Wages are distributed in direct proportion to the total amount of work done by each individual. If workers work for the same number of days, their wages are divided exactly in the ratio of their daily efficiencies.

Pipes & Cisterns

This concept is mathematically identical to Time & Work. The only difference is that an outlet pipe or leakage works with a negative efficiency (it empties the tank), while an inlet pipe works with a positive efficiency.

questions.question: Find the surface area (in cm²) of a sphere whose diameter is 21 cm.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The surface area of a sphere can be computed directly using its diameter (d) with the formula: SA = π × d².

⇒ SA = (22/7) × 21 × 21

⇒ SA = 22 × 3 × 21

⇒ SA = 66 × 21 = 1386

**∴ The correct answer is 1386 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the sphere (d) = 21 cm

Radius of the sphere (r) = d ÷ 2 = 21/2 cm

**Formula Used:**

Surface Area of a sphere = 4 × π × r²

 
 
 
• 
 
 d = 21 cm
 Sphere Surface Area

**Calculations:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × (21/2)²

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × (22/7) × (441/4)

⇒ Surface Area = (22/7) × 441

⇒ Surface Area = 22 × 63

⇒ Surface Area = 1386 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 1386 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Volume of a Sphere

The amount of space occupied by a sphere is its volume. For a sphere of radius r, Volume (V) = (4/3) × π × r³.

Hemisphere

A hemisphere is an exact half of a sphere. Its Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2 × π × r², and its Total Surface Area (TSA) is 3 × π × r².

Volume of a Hemisphere

Since it is half the size of a whole sphere, the volume of a hemisphere is given by V = (2/3) × π × r³.
</p

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought an article for ₹500. At what price (in ₹) should he sell the article to make 26% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) is considered as the base value, which is 100%.

To make a profit of 26%, the Selling Price (SP) must be 100% + 26% = 126% of CP.

SP = 126% of 500

SP = 1.26 × 500 = 630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price of the article (CP) = ₹500

Desired Profit Percentage = 26%

**Formula Used:**

Profit = (Profit% ÷ 100) × CP

Selling Price (SP) = CP + Profit

 
 CP = ₹500
 (100%)
 
 
 SP = ₹630
 (126%)
 
 

 

 + 26% Profit

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit = (26 ÷ 100) × 500

⇒ Profit = 26 × 5 = ₹130

⇒ Selling Price = CP + Profit

⇒ Selling Price = 500 + 130 = ₹630

**∴ The correct answer is ₹630.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Selling Price Formula

When the profit percentage is given, SP = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100.

Calculation for Loss

When a loss percentage is given, SP = CP × (100 − Loss%) ÷ 100.

Profit/Loss Base

Unless otherwise stated, profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: Find the third proportional of 36 and 42.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The third proportional of two numbers a and b is calculated directly using the formula: b² ÷ a.

Here, a = 36 and b = 42.

Third proportional = (42 × 42) ÷ 36

Third proportional = 1764 ÷ 36 = 49

**∴ The correct answer is 49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First number (a) = 36

Second number (b) = 42

**Formula Used:**

If c is the third proportional to a and b, they form a continuous proportion such that a : b :: b : c.

⇒ a × c = b × b

⇒ c = b² ÷ a

 

 Product of Extremes (36 × c)

 

 Product of Means (42 × 42)

 
 36

 :

 
 42

 ::

 
 42

 :

 
 c

 36 × c = 42 × 42 → c = 49

**Calculations:**

⇒ c = (42 × 42) ÷ 36

⇒ c = (7 × 6 × 7 × 6) ÷ (6 × 6)

⇒ c = 7 × 7

⇒ c = 49

**∴ The correct answer is 49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mean Proportional

The mean proportional between two numbers a and b is √(a × b).

Fourth Proportional

The fourth proportional to three numbers a, b, and c is d, such that a : b :: c : d, which simplifies to d = (b × c) ÷ a.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios a : b and c : d, their compound ratio is expressed as (a × c) : (b × d).

Duplicate Ratio

The duplicate ratio of a : b is defined as a² : b², and the sub-duplicate ratio is √a : √b.

questions.question: Ashok has ₹1612 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Raj and Varun and asked them to invest it at 8% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Raj and Varun got same amount after 15 and 16 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Ashok give to Raj?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of shares (Raj : Varun) = (1 + 8/100)¹⁶−¹⁵ = 108/100 = 27/25.

Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52 parts.

52 parts = ₹1612 ⇒ 1 part = ₹31.

Raj's share = 27 parts = 27 × 31 = ₹837.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 
 Total: ₹1612
 
 
•

• 
 
 Varun (V)
 16 Years @ 8%
 
 
• 
 
•

•

**Given:**

Total sum = ₹1612

Rate of interest (R) = 8% compounded annually

Time for Raj (T₁) = 15 years, Time for Varun (T₂) = 16 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest, A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the share of Raj be R and Varun be V.

⇒ R(1 + 8/100)¹⁵ = V(1 + 8/100)¹⁶

⇒ R / V = (1 + 8/100)¹⁶−¹⁵

⇒ R / V = (1 + 2/25)¹ = 27/25

⇒ The sum ₹1612 is divided in the ratio 27 : 25.

⇒ Total parts = 27 + 25 = 52

⇒ Value of 52 parts = ₹1612

⇒ Value of 1 part = 1612 ÷ 52 = ₹31

⇒ Raj's share = 27 parts = 27 × 31 = ₹837

**∴ The correct answer is ₹837.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equal Amounts in Compound Interest

When a sum is divided into two parts P₁ and P₂ invested at a rate R% for times T₁ and T₂ respectively such that their final amounts are equal, the ratio of their principals is given by P₁/P₂ = (1 + R/100)T²−T¹.

Effective Multiplying Factor

The multiplying factor (1 + R/100) acts as a geometric progression common ratio for every additional year the principal is invested in a compound interest scheme.

Time Difference Principle

To get equal amounts, the person who invests the money for a shorter duration must always start with a larger principal amount to compensate for the lesser interest gained over time.

Two trains are moving in opposite directions at speeds of 50 km/h and 110 km/h. The length of one train is 500 m. The time taken by them to cross each other is 12 seconds. The length (in m) of the other train, correct to 2 decimal places, is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed in opposite directions = (50 + 110) × 5/18 = 160 × 5/18 = 400/9 m/s

Total distance covered in 12 s = (400/9) × 12 = 1600/3 ≈ 533.33 m

Length of second train = Total distance − Length of first train

Length of second train = 533.33 − 500 = 33.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of first train, S₁ = 50 km/h

Speed of second train, S₂ = 110 km/h

Length of first train, L₁ = 500 m

Time taken to cross, T = 12 s

**Formula Used:**

Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂ (opposite directions)

Total Distance (L₁ + L₂) = Relative Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative Speed = 50 + 110 = 160 km/h

⇒ Relative Speed in m/s = 160 × (5 / 18) = 400 / 9 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = Speed × Time = (400 / 9) × 12

⇒ Total Distance = 1600 / 3 m ≈ 533.33 m

⇒ L₁ + L₂ = 533.33 m

⇒ 500 + L₂ = 533.33

⇒ L₂ = 533.33 − 500

⇒ L₂ = 33.33 m

**∴ The correct answer is 33.33 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two objects move towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: Relative Speed = S₁ + S₂.

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two objects move in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: Relative Speed = |S₁ − S₂|.

Unit Conversion Rule

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.

Crossing Stationary Objects

When a train crosses a pole or a standing man, the distance covered equals the length of the train itself.

questions.question: Manoj has ₹1224 with him. He divided it amongst his sons Anand and Anil and asked them to invest it at 4% rate of interest compounded annually. It was seen that Anand and Anil got same amount after 17 and 18 years respectively. How much (in ₹) did Manoj give to Anil?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For compound interest questions where final amounts are equal, the ratio of principal invested is inversely proportional to the respective multiplying factors for the time difference.

Time difference = 18 − 17 = 1 year.

Ratio of Anand's share to Anil's share = (1 + 4/100)¹ = 104/100 = 26/25.

Total parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts.

Anil's share (25 parts) = (25 ÷ 51) × 1224 = 25 × 24 = ₹600.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total amount distributed = ₹1224

Rate of Interest (R) = 4% compounded annually

Time for Anand (t₁) = 17 years

Time for Anil (t₂) = 18 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount in Compound Interest, A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

 
 Total: ₹1224
 
 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Anand (P1): 17 years
 Ratio: 26 parts
 
 
 Anil (P2): 18 years
 Ratio: 25 parts

 
• 
 
• 
 
 
 Equal Amount (A)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the principal sum given to Anand be P₁ and to Anil be P₂.

⇒ P₁(1 + 4/100)¹⁷ = P₂(1 + 4/100)¹⁸

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (1 + 4/100)¹⁸ − ¹⁷

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = (1 + 1/25)¹

⇒ P₁ / P₂ = 26 / 25

⇒ The sum of ₹1224 is divided in the ratio of 26 : 25.

⇒ Total ratio parts = 26 + 25 = 51 parts.

⇒ 51 parts = ₹1224

⇒ 1 part = 1224 ÷ 51 = 24

⇒ Anil's principal share (P₂) = 25 parts = 25 × 24 = 600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount after n years at r% compound interest per annum is derived using A = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ.

Equal Amount Rule

When a sum is split into two parts P₁ and P₂ for n₁ and n₂ years respectively such that their end amounts are exactly equal, the initial parts hold the relation P₁ / P₂ = (1 + r/100)ⁿ² − ⁿ¹.

SI vs CI Difference

The direct difference between CI and SI on the same principal is D = P(r/100)² for 2 years, and D = P(r/100)²(3 + r/100) for 3 years.

questions.question: Gopal sold 152 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 76 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let SP of 1 chair be 1 unit.

Total SP = 152 units and Profit = 76 units.

Total CP = Total SP − Profit = 152 − 76 = 76 units.

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100 = (76 ÷ 76) × 100 = 100%.

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of chairs sold = 152

Gain = Selling Price (SP) of 76 chairs

**Formula Used:**

Cost Price (CP) = SP − Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
• 
 
 CP = 76 units
 
 Profit = 76 units
 

 Total SP = 152 units
 CP + Profit = Total SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the SP of 1 chair be ₹1.

⇒ Total SP of 152 chairs = 152 × ₹1 = ₹152

⇒ Profit = SP of 76 chairs = 76 × ₹1 = ₹76

⇒ Total CP of 152 chairs = Total SP − Profit

⇒ Total CP = 152 − 76 = ₹76

⇒ Profit % = (Profit ÷ Total CP) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (76 ÷ 76) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 1 × 100 = 100%

**∴ The correct answer is 100%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Scenario

If there is a loss equal to the SP of x articles, then CP = Total SP + Loss. The loss percentage is calculated as (Loss ÷ CP) × 100.

Profit/Loss based on CP

If profit or loss is given equal to the CP of x articles, let the CP of 1 article be 1 unit, and compute the total CP and profit/loss accordingly.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always given on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount, and Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100.

questions.question: Ramesh’s expenditure in January, February, March and April was ₹28,312, ₹32,252, ₹25,012 and ₹33,500, respectively. What was his average expenditure (in ₹) during these four months?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let assumed average be ₹30,000.

Net deviation = (28312 − 30000) + (32252 − 30000) + (25012 − 30000) + (33500 − 30000)

Net deviation = −1688 + 2252 − 4988 + 3500 = −924

Average deviation = −924 ÷ 4 = −231

Actual average = 30000 − 231 = 29769

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29,769.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expenditure in January = ₹28,312

Expenditure in February = ₹32,252

Expenditure in March = ₹25,012

Expenditure in April = ₹33,500

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 
• 
 
 
 28312
 Jan

 
 32252
 Feb

 
 25012
 Mar

 
 33500
 Apr

 
• 
 Avg = 29769

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total expenditure = 28312 + 32252 + 25012 + 33500

⇒ Total expenditure = ₹119,076

⇒ Total number of months = 4

⇒ Average expenditure = 119076 ÷ 4

⇒ Average expenditure = ₹29,769

**∴ The correct answer is ₹29,769.**

**__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average

Used when different sets of data have varying frequencies. Formula: Aw = (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Combined Average

When combining multiple groups, the total average can be found by summing all values across groups and dividing by the total number of combined items.

Effect of Arithmetic Operations on Average

If a constant number is added, subtracted, multiplied, or divided across all given observations, the overall average is also modified by the exact same mathematical operation.

questions.question: A train running at 75 km/hr crosses another train running at 30 km/hr in the same direction in 108 seconds. If the length of the fast-moving train is 950 m, then what is the length (in m) of the slow-moving train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr = 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s.

Total distance covered = Relative speed × Time = 12.5 × 108 = 1350 m.

Length of slow train = Total distance − Length of fast train.

Length of slow train = 1350 − 950 = 400 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of fast train (v₁) = 75 km/hr

Speed of slow train (v₂) = 30 km/hr

Length of fast train (L₁) = 950 m

Time to cross (T) = 108 seconds

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = v₁ − v₂

Total distance = L₁ + L₂ = Relative speed × Time

 
 Fast Train: 950 m
 
• 
 

 75 km/hr
 
 
 Slow Train: L m
 
• 
 

 30 km/hr

 Relative Speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 75 − 30 = 45 km/hr

⇒ Convert km/hr to m/s: 45 × (5/18) = 12.5 m/s

⇒ Total Distance = 12.5 × 108 = 1350 m

⇒ Let the length of the slow train be L₂.

⇒ Total Distance = Length of fast train (L₁) + Length of slow train (L₂)

⇒ 1350 = 950 + L₂

⇒ L₂ = 1350 − 950 = 400 m

**∴ The correct answer is 400 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed in Opposite Directions

When two objects move in opposite directions, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds (v₁ + v₂).

Conversion of Speed Units

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.

Trains Crossing a Stationary Object

When a train crosses a stationary object with length (like a platform or bridge), the total distance covered is the length of the train plus the length of the object.
</p

Income & Expenditure Concept

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 4158 and their HCF is 54. If one of the numbers is 378, what is the other number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the property: Product of two numbers = LCM × HCF

⇒ Other Number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ Given Number

⇒ Other Number = (4158 × 54) ÷ 378

⇒ Other Number = 4158 ÷ 7 (since 378 ÷ 54 = 7)

⇒ Other Number = 594

**∴ The correct answer is 594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of the two numbers = 4158

HCF of the two numbers = 54

First number (N₁) = 378

**Formula Used:**

LCM × HCF = N₁ × N₂

**Calculation:**

⇒ 4158 × 54 = 378 × N₂

⇒ N₂ = (4158 × 54) ÷ 378

⇒ N₂ = (4158 × 54) ÷ (54 × 7)

⇒ N₂ = 4158 ÷ 7

⇒ N₂ = 594

**∴ The correct answer is 594.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM and HCF of Fractions

LCM of fractions = LCM of Numerators ÷ HCF of Denominators. HCF of fractions = HCF of Numerators ÷ LCM of Denominators.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their HCF is 1. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is always equal to their product.

Product Rule Limitation

The standard formula (LCM × HCF = Product of numbers) is valid strictly for exactly two numbers. It does not hold true for three or more numbers.
</p

questions.question: Two successive discounts of 30% and 20% was offered on food items. A man paid ₹840 for the food item. The bill amount of food item (in ₹) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net equivalent discount = A + B − (A × B) ÷ 100

⇒ Net discount = 30 + 20 − (30 × 20) ÷ 100 = 50 − 6 = 44%

Selling Price (SP) = 100% − 44% = 56% of Marked Price (MP)

⇒ 56% of Bill Amount = 840

⇒ Bill Amount = 840 × (100 ÷ 56) = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

First discount (D₁) = 30%

Second discount (D₂) = 20%

Selling price (SP) = ₹840

**Formula Used:**

SP = MP × (1 − D₁/100) × (1 − D₂/100)

 
 MP = ?
 
 
 Inter. Price
 
 
 SP = ₹840

 MP × 0.7 × 0.8 = SP

**Calculations:**

⇒ 840 = MP × (1 − 30/100) × (1 − 20/100)

⇒ 840 = MP × (70/100) × (80/100)

⇒ 840 = MP × (7/10) × (8/10)

⇒ 840 = MP × (56/100)

⇒ MP = (840 × 100) ÷ 56

⇒ MP = 1500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Equivalent Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the single equivalent discount is given by [a + b − (a × b) ÷ 100]%.

Marked Price and Selling Price

Selling Price (SP) is the price paid by the customer after deducting the discount from the initial Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is successively changed by x% and y%, the net percentage change is [x + y + (x × y) ÷ 100]%. For discounts, x and y are taken as negative values.
